connector_audit.root_cause: TerminalCandidateKind::ConnectorBoundary (the only kind ConnectorTerminalModelBuilder ever materializes into a ConnectorCandidate) is assigned exclusively to terminals owned by a ComponentCandidateKind::PrimitiveSymbol candidate (both terminal_location_detector.cpp:158 and terminal_recognizer.cpp:82 map PrimitiveSymbol -> ConnectorBoundary). Zero of the 81 current ComponentCandidates have kind PrimitiveSymbol (confirmed directly: kind distribution is diagram_furniture=47, circular_symbol=26, chassis_ground=6, enclosure=2 - PrimitiveSymbol=0). PrimitiveSymbol itself is only assigned by ComponentCandidateClassifier to a ShapeKind::Rectangle shape whose ShapeRole is NOT Enclosure; on TRX300 every detected rectangle apparently received the Enclosure role (only 2 Enclosure-kind candidates exist, 0 non-enclosure rectangles).
connector_audit.evidence_gap_classification: absent connector classification (upstream of terminal extraction and ownership) - not absence of candidate geometry (81 candidates exist), not missing terminal extraction alone, and not a missing-ownership problem. The classification path that would ever produce a connector-eligible terminal is never reached because no candidate is ever tagged PrimitiveSymbol on this diagram.

splice_audit.classification_rule: A node becomes TopologyNodeType::Junction when 3+ incidents meet or an endpoint touches a segment interior; it is promoted to Splice only if it is electrically_connective and has graph degree >= 3 after edge splitting (topology_reconstructor.cpp). This is a purely geometric/topological rule - it does not distinguish a deliberately-drawn junction dot from an incidental 3-way meeting of ordinary bus/drop-wire geometry.
splice_audit.finding: The model's 105 Splice nodes substantially exceed the 15 manually-identified genuine splice locations (7x). Every genuine drawn splice necessarily has graph degree >= 3 and would therefore be classified Splice, so the 15 real locations are very likely a SUBSET of the 105 - but the current topology provides no way to distinguish which ~15 of the 105 are the manually-identified genuine engineering splices versus ordinary multi-wire meeting points. 0 Junction-type nodes exist (consistent with AP-WIRE-029's documented, unchanged limitation that no extraction stage currently produces this type).
splice_audit.answer_q5_splices_represented: Likely all 15 are represented as a subset of the 105 raw Splice-classified nodes, but this cannot be confirmed or enumerated without additional evidence this audit did not attempt to fabricate (would require per-node visual verification against the source raster, not performed for all 105 given this AP's audit-only, non-exhaustive scope).

wire_crossing_audit.orthogonality_guarantee: MorphologyWireDetector extracts conductor geometry exclusively via a 25x1 horizontal and 1x25 vertical MORPH_RECT structuring element (morphology_detector.hpp) - by construction every ConductorSegment it produces is horizontal or vertical. ConductorNormalizer (conductor_normalizer.cpp) further classifies every segment via is_horizontal()/is_vertical() with tight tolerance (0.5px default) before merging; a segment satisfying neither is left unmerged rather than reclassified. The only code path capable of producing a genuinely diagonal ConductorSegment is GroundApproachConductorRecovery (AP-DIAG-FIX-007), and AP-DIAG-AUDIT-007 already directly verified (Section 11 of that report) that both of its diagonal/bend sub-segments are rejected by ConductorEvidenceEvaluator before joining any Wire - only the final straight run survives.
wire_crossing_audit.direction_change_at_crossings: WireReconstructor's traversal (wire_reconstructor.cpp lines ~117-124) stops unconditionally at any topology node whose incident-edge count is not exactly 2 ('A true endpoint must have exactly one incident edge. A continuation has exactly two. Any distribution node has three or more...'). A Crossing-type node always has degree 4 (two edges from each of the two crossing segments) and is therefore structurally unreachable as an intermediate hop - the walk stops before it, never continues through it. This is a pure degree check, independent of the node's `electrically_connective` flag or type label.
wire_crossing_audit.x_crossing_wire_transfer: Not possible under the current WireReconstructor algorithm for the reason above - a Wire's path can only extend through degree-2 Continuation nodes. No mechanism exists by which the reconstructor could hop from one crossing conductor to the other at an X.
wire_crossing_audit.l_corner_handling: A degree-2 node is classified Continuation only when exactly two incidents meet at that exact point (endpoint_incidents + interior_incidents == 2); WireReconstructor's walk treats it as pass-through regardless of the two segments' relative orientation, so a genuine L-corner (one horizontal segment ending exactly where a vertical segment begins) is correctly walked through as a single continuous Wire with a direction change at its own geometry, consistent with the domain rule that a wire may turn only at its own explicit corner.
wire_crossing_audit.crossing_gap_false_positives: 12 of the 28 AP-DIAG-AUDIT-008 unresolved candidates were classified suspected false positives via direct raster inspection, all matching the exact 'enclosed gap at a plain bus/grid crossing, no drawn circle' pattern AP-WIRE-FIX-002 previously and partially corrected for 3 different coordinates. This audit confirms these 12 are additional, unaddressed instances of that same known mechanism, not a new or different false-positive class.
wire_crossing_audit.answer_q7_wire_direction_change_at_inter: No - structurally impossible given the degree-2-only traversal rule verified directly in wire_reconstructor.cpp.
wire_crossing_audit.answer_q8_x_crossing_incorrect_transfer: No - same structural guarantee; Crossing nodes (degree 4) are never traversed as intermediate hops.
wire_crossing_audit.answer_q9_diagonal_segment_in_semantic_w: No - by construction of the extraction/normalization pipeline for all 35 non-recovered Wires, and by AP-DIAG-AUDIT-007's direct prior verification for the 2 AP-DIAG-FIX-007-recovered Wires (both reduced to their final straight, near-vertical run before becoming part of a Wire; the 6b6 Wire's 1px-over-15px endpoint offset is raster-quantization noise per the task's own stated exception for antialiased/corner pixels, not a diagonal engineering conductor).

answer_q10_dominant_evidence_layer: Upstream shape/symbol detection, not semantic resolution. The overwhelming majority of the 24 real components' own symbol bodies (switches, sensors, generators, relay/enclosure boxes, both fuses) never produce a ComponentCandidate at all - this is prior to and independent of SymbolFamily recognition, terminal attribution, or OCR. Where a candidate does exist (28 unresolved), the blocking evidence layer is predominantly text/OCR content (per AP-DIAG-AUDIT-008) for the few enclosure-kind candidates that were detected. Connector detection is blocked one layer further upstream still (ShapeKind/ShapeRole classification never producing a non-enclosure-rectangle PrimitiveSymbol). No single fix closes this gap: it is upstream geometry/shape classification first, then terminal-lead extraction, then text/OCR, in that order of what must exist before the next stage's absence even becomes the binding constraint.
